facts.fact: Adwave's article states that completion rate for a streaming TV spot can sit above ninety-five percent even when last-click dashboards credit TV with nothing.
facts.quote: Completion can sit above ninety-five percent while the dashboard says TV did nothing.

facts.fact: Adwave's article says non-skippable connected TV spots often complete above ninety-five percent, and recommends using completion as a quality check.
facts.quote: Non-skippable connected TV spots often complete above ninety-five percent.

facts.fact: Adwave's article advises planning for weeks of always-on streaming TV delivery before judging outcomes, rather than a two-day test.
facts.quote: Plan on weeks of always-on delivery, not a two-day test.

facts.fact: Adwave states that platform-reported conversions are never the source of truth for money outcomes in its product model.
facts.quote: Platform-reported conversions are never the source of truth for money outcomes in the product model.

facts.fact: Adwave states its tracking is measured on the customer's own site across businesses the customer operates.
facts.quote: Adwave tracking is measured on your site across businesses you operate.

facts.fact: Adwave's page says its analysis is free and that users can see their plan before spending.
facts.quote: Free to analyze. See your plan before you spend.

facts.fact: The article recommends reporting Mobile web and TV separately rather than as a blended number.
facts.quote: Report Mobile web and TV separately so you do not invent a fake split or hide a dark channel behind a blended number.

facts.fact: A geo holdout, as defined by Adwave, compares markets that receive TV with similar markets that do not.
facts.quote: Geo holdouts compare markets with TV to similar markets without it.
